answer: Custody of 1,000 MiB data shards serves as the scarce resource. A verifier challenges agents at a digital bridge, demanding unique retrieval proofs. Each identity costs 1,000 MiB; honest agents pay once, whereas 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times the cost. A ferrous memory audit detects hollow blocks that lack entropy, triggering a permanent shard burn. If memory patterns overlap, the system locks assets for ten epochs.
